findings.description: The hook is registered only on PostToolUse, which Claude Code fires only when a tool succeeds; a Bash command that exits non-zero (a failing pnpm test, tsc --noEmit with errors, a broken build) goes to PostToolUseFailure instead, so the 10k test-log threshold almost never fires on the large logs it was written for.
findings.body:
**The hook never sees the failing test, typecheck or build runs it was written for.**

Claude Code fires `PostToolUse` only when a tool succeeds. When a Bash command exits non-zero, Claude Code treats it as a tool error and sends it to `PostToolUseFailure`. That event's payload has an `error` string and no `tool_response`.

This repo already relies on that behaviour, and tests it:
- `src/core/profile-compiler.service.ts:1073-1074` says "a command that writes and then exits non-zero ends in PostToolUseFailure, not PostToolUse", and wires `PostToolUseFailure` for that reason.
- ADR 0063 says the same and has a mutation check for it.

The hook's own header gives its purpose as "cutting it would hide a failing test's output" ([tool-result-size.sh#L3](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/69e5727136925d1a21c793f462863224ebbfe835/.claude/hooks/tool-result-size.sh#L3)). But a failing `pnpm test`, a `pnpm typecheck` with errors, or a broken `pnpm build` all exit non-zero, so none of them reach this hook. A passing `vitest`/`tsc` run prints little, so the 10k `$log` branch almost never fires:

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/69e5727136925d1a21c793f462863224ebbfe835/.claude/settings.json#L126-L136

The tests can't catch this, because they pipe hand-made success payloads straight into the script.

**Suggested fix:**
- Also register the script under `PostToolUseFailure`, with the same command and timeout.
- In the jq, measure `.error` when there is no `.tool_response`, for example `(.tool_response // {stdout: .error})` feeding the Bash branch.
- Echo `.hook_event_name` back as `hookEventName` instead of hard-coding `"PostToolUse"` (line 30).
- Add a test with a `PostToolUseFailure`-shaped payload: a 15k `error` and a `pnpm test` command.

findings.description: The `pup ... (gate|test)` branch only matches the installed `pup` binary; `pnpm dev gate` (how AGENTS.md says to run the CLI from source in this repo) matches neither the `pnpm` branch (gate is not test/typecheck/build) nor the `pup` branch, so gate logs run from source get the 20k threshold instead of 10k.

The case named "a piped test run is still a test log" uses `pnpm test 2>&1`, which has no pipe, and its `&` comes after `test`, so it never checks the `[^|;&\n]*` boundary it seems meant for; there are also no cases for the Grep/Glob `filenames`, WebFetch `result`, MCP array-of-blocks, or Bash `isImage` paths the header says are counted.

Only tool_name "Bash" gets the stdout+stderr count and the log threshold; a background test run read back through BashOutput/TaskOutput (`{stdout, stderr, ...}` object, no `content`/`filenames`) falls through to the object branch and counts as 0.

The `tool_response` field names (`stdout`, `stderr`, `isImage`, `file.content`, `file.numLines`, `result`, `filenames`) are Claude Code internals, not a documented contract; if one is renamed, `try ... catch 0` counts the result as 0 and the hook silently stops warning.
The `text` helper does `.[] | .text?`; an array element that is a plain string rather than a `{text}` object yields nothing and counts as 0, undercounting the result.

The header says Bash "test, verify, typecheck and build logs" warn from 10k, but the `$log` regex on line 24 has no `verify` term (it matches `vitest`, `tsc`, `pnpm … test|typecheck|build`, `pup … gate|test`); say "pup gate" instead of "verify".

Header lines 4-7 mostly narrate what the jq does (thresholds, what is counted), which the README row already states; per AGENTS.md §Comments keep only the non-obvious WHYs (warn-only rationale, the line-number prefix counted in Read).
`tool-result-size.sh` is added to `.claude/hooks/README.md` but not to the parallel hook table and file tree in `.claude/README.md`, where every other hook is listed.
The only change here is `model: haiku` → `model: sonnet`, unrelated to the size hook and not mentioned in the PR description; split it out or explain it.

The log-command regex hardcodes `pnpm (test|typecheck|build)` etc., a second copy of TEST_CMD/TYPECHECK_CMD in `.claude/project.env` (loaded via `lib/project-env.sh`); if the project's test command changes, the 10k threshold silently stops applying.

One jq program carries size extraction, log classification and hint selection; the Read arm's `7 * numLines` is an unexplained magic number, and a named `def size:` would make the per-tool arms easier to read.
The Bash `isImage` arm and the explicit `Write or Edit then 0` arm are defensive branches; `isImage` has no test, so under the AGENTS.md Altitude rule it should get a test or be dropped.

The tests skip the 10000/10001 and 20000/20001 boundaries, the non-Bash hints (Read `offset`, other `narrow the query`), `pnpm build`/`pup gate` matches, false-positive guards such as `echo tsc`, and the Read `7 * numLines` arithmetic.

`2>/dev/null` plus `exit 0` swallows every jq failure, including a typo in the program itself, so a broken hook looks the same as a quiet one; only the positive-warning tests would catch a broken program.

process_issues.description: Every Bash call failed for the orchestrator and all seven subagents with `apply-seccomp: write /proc/self/setgroups (nested userns is capability-restricted; caller must provide CAP_SYS_ADMIN): Permission denied`. No gh or git command ran: no `gh pr view`/`gh pr diff`, no `git diff`. The review was done with Read/Grep/Glob only. Reviewers compared the PR copies in `.claude-pr/` against the in-tree base copies, which was possible only because every changed file is under `.claude/`.

The second freshness assertion (§2) could not compare HEAD against GitHub's `headRefOid`, because `gh` was unavailable. HEAD was read from `.git/refs/heads/feature/output-size-hook` as 69e5727136925d1a21c793f462863224ebbfe835, which matches the local `refs/remotes/origin/feature/output-size-hook`. A push that landed mid-review would go undetected.

PR title, body, comments and closing issues could not be read (`gh pr view` failed). Intent came from the commit message alone. No spec sources could be found, so review-spec was not spawned, and no steering context was available.

Without Bash, no one could check whether `.claude/hooks/tool-result-size.sh` has its executable bit. settings.json runs it directly by path, and `.claude/hooks/README.md` says scripts must stay executable. The test runs it via `bash "$HOOK"`, so the tests would not catch a missing bit.
